Announced himself as a former WWO Television Champion returning after three years away, accompanied by valet Talia DiMartino and bodyguard Swoll; won his own UWF debut over "Gunman" Danny Cole by pinfall (a shooting star press) on 17 November 2004. Beat Steve Ryott by pinfall (a cradle piledriver) on 25 May 2005. Talked back to Tumaffi backstage on 11 June 2005 after the big Samoan injured a try-out wrestler, then beat him by disqualification, luring him into hitting the ringpost with a chair and playing dead to fool the referee. Beat Edward Drake in the Cruiserweight Invitational Tournament's own first round on 6 July 2005 with a cradle piledriver, then exposed Tumaffi hiding under a ringside table and showed him up in retaliation for a loss to Quesada at the Road to the Gold. Lost a random-partners tag match teamed with Jason Keening against Michael Augustine and Victor Frost on 23 July 2005, pinned by a cradle brainbuster after Augustine broke up an earlier three count. Lost a Cruiserweight Invitational Tournament quarterfinal to "Hot Stuff" Brian Von Braun by submission (the Von Braun Leglock) on 18 March 2006, after a ringpost leg assault.

caption: Apex's younger brother, Miami-raised and managed by Cristine, closed out the WWO Television Championship's own surviving record as its final holder before the federation shut its doors.

A member of Sabbat Justice, billed with his brother Ravnos as the Arcana; won a six-man tag by disqualification alongside Ravnos and Avanter when an opposing wrestler struck his own partner with a chair. Teamed with Ravnos as the Arcana in a Las Vegas Street Fight win over the Fraternity Boys on 15 November 2003, pinning Brian McKenzie with a swinging DDT. Teamed with Ravnos as the Arcana again on 17 December 2003, leaping off his own brother's shoulders to plant a forearm in Bobby Lincoln's face and preserve Ravnos's own pinfall over Todd Franklin, beating the Universal Powers. Forced into a scrambled-partners tag with a reluctant Todd Franklin on 5 May 2004 against Michael Keening and Erik Grimsson; the bout ended as a no-contest after Franklin turned on him mid-match with a lariat and a swinging full nelson. Teamed with brother Ravnos, now billed together as the Amazing Romanis, to win the UWF North American Tag Team Championship from the Universal Powers (Bobby Lincoln, Todd Franklin) by pinfall on 20 October 2004, pinning Bobby Lincoln with a neckbreaker delivered off his own brother's shoulders after a returning Vyolynce's own ringside chair distraction. Teamed with brother Ravnos as the Amazing Romanis to retain the UWF North American Tag Team Championship over the Prophets of Rage (Derek Rage, Shadoe Rage) by pinfall (Without A Net) on 17 November 2004, aided by a mystery burst of pyrotechnics and an eyeball graphic that rattled Shadoe Rage ahead of the finish. Fought the Hands of Death to a no-contest defense of the UWF North American Tag Team Championship with brother Ravnos on 1 December 2004, both men later hung by dog collars. On 11 December 2004, issued a joint challenge with Ravnos to whichever of the Hands of Death or Prophets of Rage survived their own Rise to Power dog collar match.

A member of Sabbat Justice, accompanied by Tigress; his singles match against Cameron Black was ruled a no-contest after Serge Annis interfered. Returned on 22 October 2003 in a tag match against Randall Osbourne and Alex Extreme that ended without a decision after Osbourne turned on his own partner and the rest of Sabbat Justice joined a five-on-one beatdown. Reached the finals of the 17 December 2003 Meltdown Championship tournament as one of the battle royal's own final four, beat Victor Frost in the semi-finals with an inverted DDT, then beat Paul Wong in the finals with the Black Magic superbomb to become the first-ever UWF Meltdown Champion. Retained the UWF Meltdown Championship over Alex Kidd on 10 March 2004 by pinfall (Ragga Bomb) with an assist from Tigress and Randall Osbourne. Ambushed Alex Extreme and Randall Osbourne with a chair before the bell of his own 21 March 2004 title defense, a scheduled three-way, then announced grieving over his recently-deceased father and postponed the match to a cage bout the following week without the bout ever starting. Retained the UWF Meltdown Championship in the rescheduled steel cage match on 5 May 2004: Randall Osbourne never entered after Alex Kidd attacked him before the bell, and Legba climbed out of the cage to the floor ahead of Alex Extreme to win by escape. Retained the UWF Meltdown Championship again on 19 May 2004, teaming with Tigress to beat Simon O'Neal and Donna Tetreault in an intergender tag after a top-rope splash caught both opponents for the pin. Lost the UWF Meltdown Championship to Collision Holly by pinfall on 25 August 2004, caught with a second-rope bulldog after a long beating. Fought Uriah Hawkins to a double countout in a UWF Meltdown Championship tournament opener on 8 September 2004, both men brawling to the back past the referee's count. Lost a non-title three-way dance to Sabbath on 2 October 2004, pinned alongside Quinn Brown as Sabbath's Black Zero reverse hurricanrana caught him after Jessica Marshall goaded Sabbath into a rally. Escaped a Tower of Doom cage match on 30 October 2004 as part of the winning team alongside Edmond Winston IV, Victor Frost, and Luke Kinsey. Approached Chad Grimsson backstage on 27 November 2004 offering support after Lisa Drake's beating, framing himself as reformed from his own past with Sabbat Justice; the two agreed to a wary, tentative alliance. Beat Uriah Hawkins by pinfall (Roots, a fireman's carry slam counter) in a hard-fought grudge match on 11 December 2004, the two shaking hands afterward; signed a UWF North American Heavyweight Championship match against Victor Frost for Rise to Power beforehand.
